item.title: Singapore Denies The Wall Street Journal’s Probing Claims About Alice Huang Over Ties To Jensen Huang And Chinese Intelligence, “There Were No Such Investigations”
item.description:
A formal clarification has been issued by Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs, refuting The Wall Street Journal report that stated local officials were alarmed by Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang’s close relationship with former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and had investigated her as a suspected Chinese spy. In its statement, the Singapore Government flatly rejected the claims, confirming that no such investigation ever took place.

Singapore rejects claims of investigating Alice Huang over espionage concerns

To bring readers up to speed, an October 30 article from The Wall Street Journal, titled “ Chinese Executive Close to NVIDIA CEO Suspected of Giving China Information ,” cited unnamed sources claiming that Singaporean authorities were concerned about Alice Huang’s ties to Jensen Huang and had separately probed her links to China, including bringing her in for questioning in 2025.

However, Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs was having none of it, mentioning in a press release that, “We would like to make clear that neither the Singapore Government nor its officials said this. And there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang.” The ministry also published both the newspaper’s original press inquiry and the Singapore Police Force’s official response sent prior to publication.

“As would be seen from the Government response, nothing was said about Alice Huang or any concerns or investigations, regarding her alleged ties to Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang or PRC intelligence.”

While denying any investigation into Alice Huang personally, the Singapore Police Force confirmed that separate inquiries involving Singapore-based datacenter firm Megaspeed remain active. “Investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing. We are unable to comment further at this juncture.” Alice Huang was an executive at the aforementioned firm, and through her affair with Jensen Huang, she was able to construct a $7.5 billion AI GPU pipeline, with Megaspeed reportedly importing $4.6 billion in NVIDIA hardware between 2023 and 2025.

In its press release, the Singapore government reveals that The Wall Street Journal was operating on a “tight deadline” and would appreciate a timely response regarding Alice Huang. From the looks of it, the media outlet might not have been satisfied with the response and decided to push out its own narrative. To prevent false information from disseminating across the internet, we certainly hope that more authorities can come forward with clarifications like the one above so that people are properly informed about the truth.

News Source: Singapore Government

item.title: Corsair’s Unlisted 12V-2×6 Cable Packs Six Switches, One For Each 12V Pin, Letting Testers Kill Pins One By One On An RTX 5080
item.description:
Corsair has this special cable that is not available via retail channels, but demonstrates the working of its PinProtect technology.

RTX 5080 Current Testing Via Corsair's Special 12V-2x6 Cable Demonstrates How PinProtect Shuts Down the GPU After Disconnecting Five Pins

Similar to other vendors, Corsair tried to mitigate the burning and melting of the 12V-2x6 connectors through various workarounds. Its latest launch was the PinProtect technology, which launched this year alongside the new RM1200e power supply. Then we also have the PinProtect+ that was introduced with the HX1000i SHIFT Crystal power supply, which adds iCUE integration, real-time per-pin current monitoring, and configurable thresholds.

But do these features actually work? Professional Review just demonstrated this on the GeForce RTX 5080. Looks like Corsair has this special cable for testing out the feature, which has a switch hub in the middle of the 12V-2x6 cable that consists of six switches, each for the 12V pins. As you may expect, these switches can disable the individual pins, letting the current flow through the rest of the connected pins.

As of now, we haven't heard of this cable, and we couldn't find it at any retailer or on the official Corsair website. It appears that it's only used by Corsair for in-house testing, and Corsair has never announced such a product. As per the video, the user connects the RM1200e power supply to the GeForce RTX 5080 with this special cable and starts switching off individual pins one by one.

After every disconnection, the GPU continues to get stress-tested in FurMark for like 24-26 seconds. The GPU keeps pulling around 250W as it draws power from the connected pins. After connecting five of the six pins, the Corsair PinProtect triggers the GPU shutdown mechanism as a single pin exceeds the overall current it is rated to handle. PinProtect's threshold is around 9.5A per pin, and for the RTX 5080, we get around 10.5 A per pin when four of the pins are disconnected.

Of course, with the RTX 5090, the mechanism will activate much sooner due to higher power draw, and disconnecting 1-2 pins should activate PinProtect's GPU shutdown mechanism. So, the feature does work and appears to do much better than the special protective 12V-2x6 cables.

News Sources: Professional Review , Videocardz

item.title: Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Deal As Older NVIDIA GPUs No Longer Meet Its Needs
item.description:
Microsoft is reportedly winding down its AI computing agreement with Oracle , after deciding that the older-generation NVIDIA GPUs powering the rented infrastructure no longer meet its evolving requirements. The move raises further questions about the long-term economics of AI data centers, particularly as technology companies continue pouring billions into increasingly expensive hardware.

According to a November 6 report from Bloomberg , citing people familiar with the matter, Microsoft declined to renew its contract with Oracle and has gradually been switching off the rented computing capacity over recent months.

The agreement dates back to November 2023, when Oracle announced that Microsoft would leverage Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) alongside Azure to provide AI inference capabilities for Bing's conversational search engine . At the time, demand for AI accelerators was outpacing available supply, forcing even major cloud providers to seek computing resources from competitors.

However, Microsoft's requirements have since changed, and the older NVIDIA accelerators deployed in Oracle's infrastructure reportedly no longer meet its specifications. Neither the exact GPU models involved nor the financial value of the agreement has been disclosed .

Oracle Insists Older GPUs Remain Valuable

Oracle has pushed back against suggestions that aging AI hardware is becoming commercially unviable, maintaining that demand for its infrastructure remains strong.

In a statement reported by Reuters , an Oracle spokesperson emphasized that demand remains robust even for previous-generation GPUs.

The company also revealed that during its first quarter of fiscal 2027, GPU capacity coming up for renewal was renewed or resold at a 20% premium over previous contract prices , despite most of those accelerators being at least four years old. Oracle reported GPU utilization of approximately 97.9% during the same period.

This suggests that while older accelerators might no longer satisfy Microsoft's latest AI requirements, they can remain commercially viable for other customers and workloads.

Microsoft's Decision Highlights Growing Concerns Over AI Infrastructure Spending

As Fast Company recently highlighted , the development raises an uncomfortable question for companies investing heavily in AI infrastructure: what happens when expensive GPUs become technologically outdated before their associated investments have paid for themselves?

Oracle is particularly exposed to this challenge because of its enormous infrastructure expansion and substantial financing commitments.

According to its latest quarterly earnings release , Oracle generated negative $5 billion in free cash flow during Q1 FY2027, even as cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% year-over-year to $7.4 billion .

The company nevertheless continues expanding aggressively. As Wccftech previously reported , OCI has outlined plans to deploy NVIDIA's Vera Rubin systems alongside next-generation AMD, Intel, Google, and other accelerators.

Importantly, Microsoft's decision concerns a specific computing rental agreement, not the termination of its broader relationship with Oracle . The two companies maintain separate cloud partnerships, including Oracle Database@Azure .

Ultimately, the situation illustrates the increasingly difficult balance between securing sufficient AI computing capacity today and ensuring that the infrastructure remains economically competitive tomorrow. For an industry investing hundreds of billions into data centers, that distinction could become increasingly important.

News Source: Bloomberg

item.title: Intel Razor Lake Gets Its First Linux Kernel Patch Ahead Of A 2028 Launch, With Desktop Chips Expected To Reuse Nova Lake-S’s LGA 1954 Socket
item.description:
The company has begun preparing the groundwork for the next generation of consumer and server-grade CPUs.

Intel Lays Groundwork for Next-Gen Processors in Linux With Early Kernel and Compiler support

Intel is making some decent progress in delivering better support for its next-generation processors in Linux. Recently, the initial GCC patches for Coral Rapids were made, indicating support for AVX10.2, APX, AMX-FP8, AMX-AVX512, and several other advanced instructions, alongside the new AVX10_VPMLDSABFLYDQ, which aims to accelerate ML-DSA operations.

Today, Phoronix reported that Intel has started upstreaming Linux kernel support for both Coral Rapids and Razor Lake processors, which gives developers an early look at the company's upcoming CPU families. The initial patch appears basic, establishing the CPU family and model IDs, but it's the beginning of broader Linux enablement.

As per the finding, Intel engineer Tony Luck submitted the first kernel patch on November 13. Coral Rapids is identified as Family 19, Model 8 , while the Razor Lake lineup uses several Family 18 model IDs. Keep in mind that Coral Rapids is Intel's next-gen Xeon server-grade processor family, while Razor Lake will succeed Nova Lake for the mainstream consumer segment.

The Razor Lake family uses separate identifiers for the L, U, and S variants, and we expect more substantial patches in the coming weeks and months. We have been reporting on Razor Lake for a while now, as the CPU family is reportedly succeeding Nova Lake and is targeting a 2028 launch. It's expected to utilize the same LGA 1954 socket as the Nova Lake-S desktop processors .

We also reported previously that Razor Lake will introduce Griffin Cove P-Core architecture (Coral Rapids will also use it), while its higher-end variants are expected to bring significant upgrades over Nova Lake. Specs-wise, nothing significant is known yet, since the launch is pretty far away.

News Sources: Kernel , Phoronix

item.title: TeamGroup CEO Warns 2027 DRAM Shortage Could Become So Severe That Even Money Won’t Guarantee Supply
item.description:
The ongoing global memory shortage could become significantly worse in 2027, with TeamGroup warning that DRAM supplies may become so constrained that even customers willing to pay inflated prices will struggle to secure inventory .

Speaking during the Taiwanese memory manufacturer's November 2 earnings conference, TeamGroup CEO Chen Ching-wen (Gerry Chen) warned that the industry has yet to experience the worst of the current memory crisis.

According to Taiwan's Economic Daily News , Chen expects the most severe supply constraints to occur between Q4 2026 and the end of Q2 2027 , with little indication of meaningful price reductions throughout next year.

The executive also cautioned that supply and demand may not return to equilibrium until the second half of 2028 at the earliest .

Even money can't buy goods.

Chen's warning reflects a market increasingly dominated by AI infrastructure investment, where securing sufficient memory capacity has become almost as challenging as managing its rapidly rising cost.

AI Demand Is Squeezing DRAM Supplies While Prices Continue To Skyrocket

One of the biggest contributors to the shortage is the rapid expansion of AI data centers, which consume enormous quantities of high-bandwidth memory (HBM ) and conventional server DRAM.

Major manufacturers, including Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron , have increasingly prioritized higher-margin HBM and enterprise memory production, leaving less capacity available for consumer DDR, LPDDR, and GDDR products.

According to TrendForce , HBM manufacturing requires substantially more wafer input than conventional DRAM , further restricting the industry's ability to meet demand.

The impact is already evident in TeamGroup's own operations. According to the company's November 2026 investor presentation , business-to-business sales accounted for 64.6% of revenue during the first nine months of 2026 , compared to just 24.6% during the corresponding period last year.

TeamGroup also reported record quarterly revenue of approximately NT$10.14 billion , alongside an impressive gross margin of 49.27% .

Meanwhile, some server memory spot prices are reportedly 30% to 50% higher than their contractual counterparts , illustrating just how difficult obtaining additional inventory has become.

According to figures cited by Tom's Hardware , contract prices for a 16-gigabit (2-gigabyte) DDR5 chip climbed from approximately $8.70 in October 2025 to $48 in September 2026 , representing an increase of more than fivefold . These are chip-level prices rather than retail prices for complete memory modules.

Memory Shortages Could Persist Well Beyond 2027

Unfortunately, expanding manufacturing capacity is unlikely to provide immediate relief.

Although new facilities and production upgrades are underway, TrendForce expects meaningful additions to DRAM supply to remain limited until 2028 . The firm also anticipates continued price pressure throughout 2027, although it expects NAND flash supply conditions to improve sooner .

This outlook echoes an earlier warning from SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung , who predicted that 2027 could represent the industry's worst-ever memory supply shortage, with demand potentially exceeding his company's production capacity even beyond 2030 .

As Wccftech previously reported , Samsung and SK hynix have already experienced exceptionally low memory inventories amid accelerating AI demand.

For PC gamers and enthusiasts considering future memory and GPU upgrades, TeamGroup's forecast suggests that high RAM prices and constrained availability may remain serious concerns throughout 2027 . However, these projections remain uncertain and will depend heavily on AI spending, consumer demand, and the pace at which new manufacturing capacity becomes available.

News Source: Economic Daily News

item.title: GeForce RTX 5090 And RTX 5080 Witness A Sudden Price Drop Of Up To 22% In Japan, But It’s Unlikely Due To Jensen’s Resignation
item.description:
A lot has happened in the past few days, but the sudden price decline for some of the high-end RTX 50 series GPUs was unexpected.

Japan Records An Unexpected Price Drop For RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 GPUs Right After Jensen's Resignation, But No Direct Connection Between the Two

NVIDIA might not remain the same after Jensen's resignation. After 33 years of work at the company, Jensen decided to step down , and with the company's leadership now entering a transition period, it remains to be seen how the change will affect GeForce and NVIDIA's gaming business going forward. That said, following Jensen's resignation, we are witnessing an unexpected and sudden drop in prices for some of the best gaming GPUs.

Multiple Japanese outlets have reported that the prices of the flagship RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 have suddenly dropped the next day following Jensen's resignation. Japanese retailer Dospara ( Kakaku.com as the price-comparison platform) shows that some RTX 5090 GPUs, like the Palit RTX 5090 GameRock 32 GB card, have dropped from 1,288,000 Yen ($8062) to 1,048,000 Yen ($6560) in a single day, which is a solid 18.6% reduction in price.

However, ITmedia reports that the same GPU at its Akihabara store got a solid 22.38% reduction and now sits under 1M Yen ( 999,800 Yen exactly). As far as the GeForce RTX 5080 is concerned, the GPU was selling for over 300,000 Yen and peaked at 359,800 Yen a few days ago. The GPU now sits at 299,800 Yen or US$1876 , which is a 16.7% reduction in price. So, both high-end GPUs received some substantial discounts following Jensen's stepping down as the CEO.

However, we couldn't find any direct relation between the two, as Gazlog reports that the prices for these cards had already peaked at the end of October. The RTX 5080 was reportedly already declining in price after that, and as the 300,000+ Yen price tags were hurting sales , the inventory was building up at the same time, which resulted in significant price cuts.

At the same time, the RTX 5090 supply inventory returned around November 3, and other retailers got their supplies alongside Dospara. Subsequently, the RTX 5090 also saw some decent price cuts.

News Sources: Gazlog , @pcbuildnet , ITmedia

item.title: Intel Reclaims 70% Desktop CPU Market Share As AMD Falls Below 30% In Surprise Q3 2026 Turnaround
item.description:
Intel has staged a rather unexpected comeback in the desktop CPU market, reclaiming a significant portion of the market share it previously lost to AMD. Interestingly, the turnaround might have more to do with supply conditions and the struggling gaming PC market than a sudden shift in processor competitiveness.

According to the latest Q3 2026 figures from Mercury Research , shared by PC Gamer , Intel's desktop x86 CPU shipment share climbed to 70.1%, up from 65.1% in the preceding quarter. Meanwhile, AMD's share declined from 34.9% to just 29.9% , representing a roughly five-percentage-point swing in Intel's favor .

This is particularly surprising considering AMD's recent momentum. As we reported back in August , Intel's overall x86 CPU market share had fallen to levels last seen in 1995, while AMD continued gaining ground across several segments.

So, what explains this rather dramatic reversal?

Mercury Research acknowledges that the exact causes remain uncertain, but suggests Intel may have redirected more processor supply toward the desktop market following weaker demand for mobile CPUs . With desktop CPU demand typically increasing during the third quarter, Intel appears to have benefited from a seasonal recovery after undersupplying the segment earlier in 2026.

AMD, on the other hand, apparently failed to capitalize on the same seasonal uptick.

Another possible explanation concerns AMD's stronger exposure to the enthusiast gaming market. Despite the company's Ryzen X3D processors maintaining a considerable gaming-performance advantage, Mercury Research suggests that supply constraints affecting gaming GPUs have weakened demand for gaming PCs, disproportionately impacting AMD .

Rising DRAM prices could be exacerbating the situation. Indeed, Intel's own Q3 2026 filing confirms that higher component costs, particularly memory, have negatively impacted client demand . Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenue actually declined 5% year-over-year despite its desktop shipment-share gains .

Meanwhile, AMD's latest financial results highlight the company's increasing dependence on its lucrative data center business, which generated a record $8.5 billion in quarterly revenue, up 97% year-over-year .

Notably, AMD continued gaining ground in server CPU shipments , with its share increasing from 34.5% to 35.5% during Q3 2026 , suggesting that its broader competitive position remains relatively strong.

Ultimately, Intel's desktop market-share rebound should not necessarily be interpreted as a sudden resurgence in gaming CPU competitiveness. These figures measure processor shipments rather than end-user purchases, and the company's gains could reflect improved supply availability and shifting market demand rather than consumers abandoning AMD's Ryzen processors.

News Source: PC Gamer

item.title: GeForce Evangelist Jacob Freeman Assures Consumers That The Future Of Gaming GPUs Is Safe, But That Doesn’t Mean Graphics Cards Will Become Cheaper
item.description:
It has certainly been a wild week, and with Jensen Huang’s exit as NVIDIA CEO , there’s an elephant-sized uncertainty concerning the future of the GeForce brand and, in general, the future of gaming. Fortunately, Evangelist Jacob Freeman has come forward to clear the air of confusion, and after being asked whether NVIDIA was going to continue forward without gaming GPUs, he gave some much-needed reassurance to those who were contemplating switching to AMD or Intel.

“Nope” is the reply that Freeman gave after being asked whether NVIDIA will cut the GeForce brand from its lineup

Posting on X while attending PDXLAN, one of North America’s largest LAN gaming events, Freeman acknowledged the recent upheaval surrounding the company while emphasizing that NVIDIA’s commitment to PC gaming remains intact. Alongside photos celebrating the brand’s long-standing presence at the event, Freeman wrote, “A lot has happened this week. I’m grateful to work alongside some amazing colleagues who love PC gaming, hardware, and tech. This work continues!”

When another X user directly asked, “Hey Jacob, lots of people are saying this is the end of geforce. Thoughts?” Freeman shut down the speculation with a blunt, one-word response: “Nope.” We’re confident that this reply alone will echo a sigh of relief across millions of NVIDIA gaming GPU owners who were potentially sweating over the possibility that they won’t foresee the chance to upgrade to the RTX 6000 series, which is unlikely to launch in 2027 .

However, while the GeForce brand won’t be going anywhere, consumers are likely going to have to weather long wait times amid a supply crunch and have to dig deep into their wallets, because Freeman’s confirmation doesn’t guarantee that NVIDIA’s RTX 6000 series of consumer graphics cards will be affordable or available in abundance. In fact, given how the RTX 5090’s price has soared to $9,000, or a 370 percent increase from its original MSRP of $1,999, gamers should brace themselves for the same outcome materializing in 2028.

After all, the AI boom means that gaming GPUs aren’t safe from the semiconductor shortage, and even if NVIDIA gives slight importance to the RTX 6000 lineup’s production, nothing is stopping these graphics cards from either being picked up in bulk from third-party sellers and sold at insane markups, or ending up landing in China, where top-end GPUs like the RTX 5090 are having their coolers re-purposed to fit in AI servers , while also having their PCBs modded to accommodate 96GB VRAM .

News Source: Jacob Freeman

Ubisoft has given the go-ahead to Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Vegas 3 , according to a report published by Insider Gaming's Tom Henderson . The insider has heard that Ubisoft Montréal has just spun off three new projects , one of which is the return of this particular version of the Rainbow Six franchise.

The original Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006 for PC, Xbox 360, and PlayStation 3. It was a major reinvention of the once PC-only tactical shooter IP , borrowing several aspects from the most popular shooters of the time, such as regenerating health and unlimited squad revives. It also added a seamless first-to-third-person cover system , which smoothly transitioned the camera from first-person to a third-person over-the-shoulder view and back to first-person once out of cover. This allowed players to peek around corners, survey rooms safely, and blind-fire over cover .

Rainbow Six Vegas levels made heavy use of vertical combat spaces . Players and AI squadmates could rappel down casino facades, elevator shafts, and glass skylights, and even flip upside down into an inverted rappel to breach upper-story windows and clear rooms from unexpected angles. A persistent progression system unified unlocks across all modes, and of course, the Las Vegas setting brought a refreshing take on the usually nondescript Rainbow Six maps.

The game was highly successful and spawned a sequel that launched in 2008. While still well received, it was widely deemed too similar to the predecessor . When the franchise made its triumphant return in 2015 with Siege , it went in an entirely different direction.

Ubisoft's decision to return to Rainbow Six Vegas after nearly two decades since the last entry likely signals a desire to revive at least some elements of the predecessors, though it may be several years before we hear any concrete details. Meanwhile, a single-player turn-based spin-off titled Rainbow Six Tactics was announced at Gamescom 2026 .

item.title: Elon Musk Says Petition To Bring Jensen Huang Back To NVIDIA Is Underway And He’ll Sign It
item.description:
Tesla and SpaceX billionaire Elon Musk, who has previously supported bringing former NVIDIA CEO and founder Jensen Huang back to the firm as chairman, is now going to sign a petition in Huang's favor. Musk's comments come after Huang admitted to having a deeply personal relationship with a Singaporean data center executive of a firm under scrutiny for having smuggled AI chips to China.

Musk's Remarks Come After Former NVIDIA CEO Abruptly Resigned Under Controversial Circumstances

Musk's announcement, which makes him the only major technology executive to have come out in support of Huang, comes as some voices in the open source AI camp also begin to voice their support of the CEO who bought Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.

While the SpaceX CEO, who works closely with NVIDIA for procuring millions of GPUs for his mega data centers and who has made NVIDIA the exclusive supplier of AI chips to his firm, hasn't mentioned open-source AI, he has supported opinions of Huang being irreplaceable for American AI leadership.

The abrupt exit of a CEO of a multi-trillion-dollar company also brought criticism from former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton. In a podcast, Clinton shared that counterintelligence protocol requires informing an American citizen of a honeypot operation. However, as per CNN, US intelligence remained unclear about the link between Huang's associate, Alice Huang and Chinese intelligence agencies.

Given his previous support of Huang, Musk's latest announcement that not only is a petition underway to reinstate the former CEO but that he was signing it as well is unsurprising. They follow an earlier letter allegedly sent by NVIDIA employees to their leadership, but whether the upcoming petition will involve employees is unclear.

Focus on Huang's associate Alice Huang being a spy came while her firm Megaspeed was being scrutinized for having smuggled chips to China. Megaspeed isn't the only company Alice Huang is related to, as she also set up a company in China that later disclosed having access to banned NVIDIA chips in a data center in Shanghai.

While Musk's petition is being prepared, the reasons behind Huang's departure have continued to generate speculation. As the open source camp remembers him fondly, reports have also claimed that the executive was worried about over-selling AI computing GPUs .

item.title: Apex Neural Rendering vs. NVIDIA DLSS: We Test 2X, 3X, And 4X (Multi) Frame Generation In Three PC Games
item.description:
AI-powered frame generation has rapidly become one of the most important technologies in modern PC gaming. By inserting artificially generated frames between those traditionally rendered by the game engine, technologies such as NVIDIA DLSS (Multi) Frame Generation , Intel XeSS (Multi) Frame Generation, or FSR Frame Generation can considerably improve perceived fluidity, particularly in graphically demanding games.

However, frame generation isn't without its shortcomings. Visual artifacts, inconsistent frame pacing, additional processing overhead, and input latency can all negatively affect the gaming experience, especially as higher multi frame generation (MFG) multipliers are introduced.

Enter Apex Neural Rendering (ANR) , an emerging alternative developed by Apex Compute that promises superior image quality, faster frame generation processing, and substantially lower GPU memory consumption compared to NVIDIA DLSS (M)FG.

But can this newcomer actually challenge NVIDIA's established solution?

To investigate, we're testing ANR (M)FG against NVIDIA DLSS (M)FG in Valor Mortis , Cyberpunk 2077 , and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered , evaluating conventional 2X frame generation alongside more demanding 3X and 4X multi frame generation.

We'll examine image quality through our own gameplay recordings and compare performance using CapFrameX 's Display Times metrics, including average FPS, 1% lows, 0.1% lows, and PC latency .

What Is Apex Neural Rendering?

As we previously reported , Apex Neural Rendering is an AI-powered rendering suite comprising three technologies: Frame Generation (FG), Super Resolution (SR), and Ray Reconstruction (RR) .

Currently, only ANR Frame Generation is publicly available in beta , including support for Multi Frame Generation. The remaining two components are expected to receive beta releases later, and we may cover them separately once they're available.

Unlike NVIDIA DLSS, ANR promises broad compatibility with older hardware, including GeForce GTX 16 and RTX 20 Series GPUs onward, Radeon RX 5000 Series GPUs onward, and Intel Arc graphics cards .

According to Apex Compute's official benchmarks , ANR FG consumes just 214 MB of GPU memory at 4K, compared to 562 MB for NVIDIA DLSS FG , representing a reduction of approximately 62%.

The developer also claims up to 2.4X faster frame-generation processing in selected workloads, alongside higher image-quality scores across CGVQM-5, ColorVideoVDP, and PSNR measurements .

However, those are internal benchmarks, and improvements in frame generation processing time don't necessarily translate into equivalent gains in actual gaming FPS .

That's precisely why independent comparisons are important.

How To Download And Install ANR

ANR can be downloaded from Apex Compute's official GitHub repository , which provides installation packages for games with and without OptiScaler .

For our tests, we're using ANR FG V.B15 , released on November 12, which addresses a VRAM leak that could occur when games repeatedly reinitialized Frame Generation.

The full package, anr-fg-V.B15-full.zip , already includes OptiScaler, so a separate installation isn't necessary .

After extracting the archive, close the game and run the included install.cmd script, pointing it toward the folder containing the game's executable .

ANR integrates through OptiScaler, intercepting the game's Frame Generation implementation and replacing it with its own neural interpolation model.

Once installed, simply launch the game and enable DLSS Frame Generation through the graphics settings. ANR automatically takes over without requiring an additional hotkey.

Users can confirm that ANR initialized correctly by checking the nr_fg-*.log files inside the game's OptiScaler/custom/Apex Neural Rendering FG folder.

To remove ANR, run the included uninstall.cmd script against the same game directory.

Enabling Multi Frame Generation On Older GeForce RTX GPUs

Since our test system uses a GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, which officially supports only conventional 2X DLSS Frame Generation, we'll also be using dashdogy's Universal MFG Unlocker .

This community-developed modification enables higher DLSS Multi Frame Generation multipliers on compatible older GeForce GPUs, including RTX 40 Series hardware.

Interestingly, Hardware Unboxed recently tested NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation on a modded GeForce RTX 3090 against an RTX 5090 , finding v irtually identical interpolation quality, including matching visual artifacts, alongside smooth and consistent frame pacing . The channel also successfully demonstrated higher Multi Frame Generation multipliers on the older Ampere GPU, challenging NVIDIA's official hardware restrictions. These findings suggest that DLSS FG/MFG can operate comparably on older architectures, including Ada Lovelace and our RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, although identical performance and latency across different GPUs aren't guaranteed .

For our comparisons, we'll evaluate matching frame generation multipliers between NVIDIA DLSS and ANR, with 3X and 4X configurations enabled through the appropriate modified integration.

Our Testing Methodology

All tests are conducted on an ASUS TUF Gaming F15 laptop, featuring the following hardware:

To compare actual displayed frame delivery, we're using CapFrameX's MsBetweenDisplayChange (Display Times) metric , rather than relying exclusively on conventional application frame time measurements.

This is particularly important for frame generation, where the displayed frame rate can be considerably higher than the rate at which the game engine processes simulation and player inputs.

Our performance measurements include average displayed FPS, 1% and 0.1% lows, stuttering, and CapFrameX's experimental PC latency figures .

We have approximately 20-second benchmark captures for each implementation in the following configurations:

  • Valor Mortis : DLSS FG 2X vs. ANR FG 2X.
  • Cyberpunk 2077 : DLSS MFG 3X vs. ANR MFG 3X.
  • The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered : DLSS MFG 4X vs. ANR MFG 4X.

Each game will also feature three separate YouTube video comparisons at 2X, 3X, and 4X. These additional videos focus on visual differences, while the CapFrameX benchmarks discussed below correspond to the specific multipliers listed above.

Also, keep in mind that YouTube's video compression can obscure fine details and introduce additional artifacts , making these frame generation comparisons more difficult to evaluate accurately. Unfortunately, it's an unavoidable compromise when sharing gameplay footage through the platform.

The short capture durations mean the results should be interpreted as indicative rather than comprehensive statistical measurements, especially when examining rare frame time spikes.

Valor Mortis — DLSS FG 2X vs. ANR FG 2X

We'll begin with Valor Mortis , the first-person action RPG from One More Level , the developer behind the Ghostrunner series.

Here, we'll be testing conventional 2X frame generation, comparing NVIDIA DLSS FG 2X against ANR FG 2X under identical conditions.

Video Comparison

We began our comparison with Valor Mortis at 2X Frame Generation , and the initial results were rather encouraging for ANR. Motion interpolation quality proved surprisingly comparable to NVIDIA DLSS FG, with both implementations delivering convincing results and reasonably fluid motion during gameplay. Flickering, ghosting, and other interpolation artifacts were generally well-controlled, making the visual differences between the two technologies relatively minor. However, this could represent something of a best-case scenario for ANR , as conventional 2X frame generation only generates one additional frame between traditionally rendered frames, potentially masking temporal instability and interpolation artifacts that might become more pronounced at higher MFG multipliers. Overall, it's a promising start for Apex Compute's technology, although more demanding tests await.

Performance And Frame Pacing

Our CapFrameX benchmarks reveal an interesting trade-off between average performance and frame pacing consistency. ANR FG achieves 170.6 average displayed FPS versus NVIDIA DLSS FG's 153.7 FPS, representing an impressive 11% improvement. However, this advantage quickly evaporates when examining lower-percentile performance.

NVIDIA maintains considerably stronger 1% lows at 54.7 FPS versus ANR's 41.3 FPS , while the 0.1% lows reveal an even greater discrepancy: 33.2 FPS for DLSS versus just 18.5 FPS for ANR , a substantial 44% regression. The frame time graphs reinforce these findings, with ANR exhibiting more severe spikes and approximately twice as much time classified as stuttering ( 3.5% versus 1.8% ).

On the other hand, reported PC latency is remarkably close, with ANR slightly ahead at 35.5 ms versus NVIDIA's 37.5 ms .

Ultimately, ANR delivers higher average FPS, but NVIDIA DLSS maintains a substantial advantage in lower-percentile performance and frame pacing consistency. Interestingly, these differences weren't nearly as apparent during our visual comparisons, where both implementations felt relatively comparable in terms of motion fluidity.

Cyberpunk 2077 — DLSS MFG 3X vs. ANR MFG 3X

Next up is Cyberpunk 2077 , one of the most technically impressive games available on PC.

Its dense environments, advanced lighting, moving vehicles, animated characters, and sophisticated ray tracing provide numerous opportunities for interpolation artifacts.

For our primary performance comparison, we'll be using 3X Multi Frame Generation , with two generated frames inserted between consecutive traditionally rendered frames.

Video Comparison

Unfortunately, Cyberpunk 2077 at 3X Multi Frame Generation paints a considerably less flattering picture for ANR . Compared to NVIDIA DLSS MFG, ANR exhibits noticeably more flickering, poorer temporal stability, and substantially more interpolation artifacts, particularly during camera movement . Motion also feels considerably more jittery and less fluid , undermining the benefits of the additional generated frames. Making matters worse, ANR doesn't interpolate HUD/UI elements in our tested configuration , leaving them updating at the considerably lower base rendering frame rate while the surrounding game world appears smoother. This discrepancy becomes especially jarring at higher MFG multipliers, where the gap between rendered and displayed frames grows even wider. Ultimately, ANR falls well short of Apex Compute's promises of superior interpolation quality in Cyberpunk 2077 , which is quite disappointing following its more encouraging showing in Valor Mortis .

Performance And Frame Pacing

Cyberpunk 2077 presents a much closer contest, at least from a purely numerical standpoint. ANR MFG averages 224.1 displayed FPS compared to NVIDIA DLSS MFG's 218.8 FPS , a modest 2.4% advantage.

The 1% lows are virtually identical at 108.3 FPS for ANR versus 109.2 FPS for DLSS . However, NVIDIA maintains a more noticeable lead in the 0.1% lows, achieving 73.3 FPS compared to ANR's 64.7 FPS , representing an approximately 12% deficit for the latter.

Both implementations demonstrate relatively consistent frame delivery throughout most of their respective captures, with only occasional frame time spikes. CapFrameX reports minimal stuttering for either technology, at approximately 0.2% for DLSS and 0.3% for ANR . Interestingly, ANR also reports slightly lower PC latency at 41.8 ms versus NVIDIA's 45.3 ms , a reduction of 3.5 milliseconds .

On paper, Cyberpunk 2077 is essentially a draw , with ANR offering marginally higher average FPS and lower reported latency, while DLSS maintains slightly stronger lows. However, these figures don't tell the whole story. As our earlier visual comparison demonstrated, ANR's noticeably inferior temporal stability, increased flickering, and jitterier motion make NVIDIA DLSS MFG the more convincing solution during actual gameplay .

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered — DLSS MFG 4X vs. ANR MFG 4X

For our final comparison, we're returning to the Continent with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered .

Released in September 2026, the visual overhaul introduced Path Tracing, NVIDIA DLSS 4.5, improved lighting, upgraded vegetation, and numerous other enhancements.

The game's expansive forests, dense foliage, horseback traversal, and elaborate character animations provide a particularly demanding workload for frame generation.

This time, we're pushing both implementations to 4X Multi Frame Generation , inserting three generated frames between each pair of traditionally rendered frames.

Video Comparison

Our final comparison, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered at 4X Multi Frame Generation, delivers decidedly mixed results . On the positive side, ANR virtually eliminates the distracting screen-edge tearing and wavy distortions that plague NVIDIA DLSS MFG , resulting in a noticeably cleaner image during camera movement, especially around dense foliage and fine environmental details. Unfortunately, this improvement comes with some significant compromises. ANR's motion interpolation feels noticeably less fluid and more jittery than NVIDIA's implementation , with inconsistent frame delivery undermining the perceived smoothness of the generated frames. Furthermore, the non-interpolated HUD/UI elements become particularly distracting at 4X, as they continue updating at the much lower base rendering frame rate while the surrounding environment benefits from Multi Frame Generation . Ultimately, while ANR deserves credit for addressing one of NVIDIA DLSS MFG's most frustrating visual shortcomings, its inferior perceived smoothness and inconsistent HUD presentation make it difficult to recommend over NVIDIA's implementation in its current state.

Performance And Frame Pacing

Our final benchmark delivers perhaps the most intriguing results of the three. ANR MFG achieves 277.5 average displayed FPS versus NVIDIA DLSS MFG's 259.9 FPS , representing a respectable 6.8% improvement.

NVIDIA nevertheless maintains stronger 1% lows at 162.5 FPS compared to ANR's 151.7 FPS . Interestingly, the situation reverses in the 0.1% lows, where ANR achieves 75.0 FPS versus NVIDIA's 56.7 FPS , an improvement of approximately 32% .

Both implementations exhibit occasional frame time spikes, although NVIDIA's most severe excursions appear more pronounced. CapFrameX also identifies slightly less time classified as stuttering with ANR, at 0.3% versus NVIDIA's 0.4% .

However, PC latency tells a dramatically different story . ANR reports an average of 57.8 ms compared to just 38.6 ms for NVIDIA DLSS MFG, representing an increase of 19.2 milliseconds , or nearly 50% . While CapFrameX's experimental latency measurements warrant further verification, this discrepancy is substantial enough to raise concerns about responsiveness.

Ultimately, ANR delivers higher average FPS and stronger 0.1% lows, but its considerably higher reported latency and inferior perceived motion smoothness undermine those advantages . Combined with the distracting non-interpolated HUD elements discussed earlier, the results reinforce why higher displayed frame rates don't necessarily translate into a better gaming experience .

Final Words

Apex Neural Rendering shows promise, but our testing reveals that it still has a long way to go before challenging NVIDIA DLSS FG/MFG. While ANR consistently delivers higher average displayed FPS across all three games, these gains don't necessarily translate into smoother gameplay or superior image quality.

Valor Mortis represents ANR's strongest showing, with motion interpolation quality comparable to DLSS FG at 2X, albeit with noticeably weaker lows . However, the cracks become apparent at higher multipliers. In Cyberpunk 2077 , ANR MFG suffers from excessive flickering, poorer temporal stability, and noticeably jitterier motion . The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered presents a mixed picture: ANR largely eliminates NVIDIA's distracting screen-edge distortions, but its inferior perceived smoothness, non-interpolated HUD elements, and nearly 50% higher reported PC latency undermine that advantage .

Ultimately, ANR's higher FPS figures fail to compensate for its inconsistent interpolation quality and frame delivery , particularly at 3X and 4X. Although its broad hardware compatibility and reduced screen-edge artifacts are commendable, NVIDIA DLSS remains the more polished solution overall . ANR is still in beta, however, and with Super Resolution and Ray Reconstruction also on the horizon, Apex Compute has plenty of opportunities to improve its technology.

item.title: Letter Seeking Ex CEO Jensen Huang’s Return Is “Obviously Fake,” Says NVIDIA VP After He Is Made A Named Signatory Alongside Top Leadership At Firm
item.description:
The vice president of NVIDIA's applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, has revealed that he did not sign a letter circulating online addressed to NVIDIA's board to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang. Huang's sudden resignation from the firm that is the driving force behind global AI development has divided the technology industry, and a copy of a letter making online rounds lists others, such as NVIDIA's chief AI scientist, Bill Dally.

Fake Letter Claims Top NVIDIA Leadership Wants Management To Bring Former CEO & Founder Jensen Huang Back To The Company

Catanzaro's remarks come after a report from Wired shared that more than 1,600 employee racked up in support of the former executive on the firm's internal communications channels. NVIDIA has 42,000 employees worldwide and the vast majority of them work in the firm's research and development division.

Following the report, an alleged letter in Jensen Huang's support racked up hefty views on social media platform X. Signed by top leadership at the firm, including accelerated computing president Ian Buck and chief scientist Bill Dally, it expressed shock at Huang's removal and threatened rebellion by securing jobs at SpaceX.

In fact, as software developer Daniel Zhang pointed out, the letter with signatures including that of Catanzaro, resembles the one OpenAI's leadership wrote to the board following Sam Altman's firing in 2023.

As for the applied deep learning research VP, he didn't hold back and commented :

"There is a made-up letter circulating online asking NVIDIA’s board to reinstate Jensen, claiming my involvement. This letter is obviously fake, and even if it were real I would not sign it.

I am grief-stricken that Jensen is no longer with NVIDIA. At the same time, I fully support NVIDIA’s board and have confidence in their decisions.

I’ve worked with Colette for years and know her as an extraordinary leader. She has my full support."

Others, particularly in the open source AI community, have also expressed support for Huang. These include the CEO of artificial intelligence-based code generation firm Replit, Amjad Masad and Hugging Face co-founder and CEO, Clement Delangue.

NVIDIA's interim CEO, Colette Kress, has worked at the firm for 13 years and briefed investors alongside Huang at the firm's earnings calls. Huang's departure has led to speculation about NVIDIA's supply chain capacity procurement and the difficult task of finding a replacement who matches his insights.

item.title: SteamOS 3.9.6 Beta Fixes A Bug Where A 30 FPS Game With A 60 FPS Cap Dropped To 24 FPS On 120 Hz Displays
item.description:
The latest beta addresses several display and frame-pacing problems alongside fixing HDR10 colors and other bugs.

Valve Improves Frame Pacing, 240 Hz+ Display Support, and HDR10 Output in its Latest SteamOS Beta

Valve is making some substantial progress in improving the experience on its SteamOS, and it's evident from the release notes of its latest 3.9.6 Beta release. The new version brings several improvements, particularly those that help make gaming a smoother experience while also fixing several issues associated with high refresh rate displays and HDR output.

The update is currently available through Beta and Preview channels. According to the release notes, the most notable change is the improved frame timing when using the built-in frame-rate limiter with Variable Refresh Rate or VRR. Valve has improved the frame timing when the limiter is used without VRR, which should help games deliver more consistent frame pacing instead of uneven frame delivery.

Valve highlighted a problem where a capped game could run below its expected frame rate on a fixed-refresh display. For instance, a 30 FPS game running with a 60 FPS limit on a 120 Hz display could previously drop to 24 FPS, but SteamOS 3.9.6 addresses this behavior. The update also fixes games running below the display's refresh rate on 240 Hz and higher refresh rate monitors.

That is particularly beneficial for gamers who are running SteamOS on desktop systems or hardware connected to high-refresh-rate monitors. Surely, this doesn't mean that the games will now hit 240 FPS, but the update is fixing situations where the OS incorrectly prevents games from reaching the available refresh rate.

Another notable fix is related to the HDR10 output. There was an issue where the SDR content could appear oversaturated when HDR10 was enabled on displays that do not feature a wide color gamut. The latest version 3.9.6 should now deliver more accurate colors when switching between SDR and HDR content.

Apart from these fixes, Valve has introduced many more, such as Steam Remote Play no longer displaying a green screen on NVIDIA GPUs. The update also fixes a black-screen problem that was affecting some RPG Maker games using Fullscreen++, alongside several rare crashes and memory errors.

News Sources: Steam , Techpowerup

item.title: Instead Of Lowering GPU Prices, Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Financed AI Startups To Absorb Excess Silicon, Shattering The Shortage Perception
item.description:
How We Rate Rumors
  • 0-20%: Unlikely - Lacks credible sources
  • 21-40%: Questionable - Some concerns remain
  • 41-60%: Plausible - Reasonable evidence
  • 61-80%: Probable - Strong evidence
  • 81-100%: Highly Likely - Multiple reliable sources
RUMOR ASSESSMENT

75%

Probable

Source 5/5

Corroboration 3/5

Technical 4/5

Timeline 3/5

Now that NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang is no longer the company CEO , we have some truth behind the exponential rise of semiconductor and memory prices. According to the latest findings, it appears that we were led to believe that there was an organic supply shortage, but in reality, we learn that Jensen was actually leveraging NVIDIA’s own balance sheet to finance AI startups and datacenter buildouts so they could absorb the company’s over-ordered semiconductor shipments from TSMC.

NVIDIA faced an “avalanche” of excess TSMC silicon and memory, and the only way to curb the oversupply was to fund AI startup

The fresh revelations stem from a tense August 2026 confrontation between Huang and NVIDIA’s longtime Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, now the interim CEO. Seeing as how the former head honcho was escalating the GPU maker’s financial exposure, Kress pushed to rein in the company’s “circular financing” commitments to smaller cloud providers and major AI firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Initial discussions had floated underwriting roughly 8 gigawatts of OpenAI compute valued at up to $250 billion, and Kress successfully scaled NVIDIA’s signed guarantee cap down to roughly 4.25 gigawatts, or up to $125 billion. As a result, Jensen reportedly belittled Kress for questioning the deals, referring to her as “a deer in the headlights.”

To justify NVIDIA's need to financially underwrite OpenAI and smaller cloud operators to keep them purchasing its GPUs, Huang privately admitted that major cloud giants were pivoting away from NVIDIA in favor of in-house custom chips. With hyperscalers actively reducing their reliance on “off-the-shelf parts,” Huang acknowledged that the massive volume of prepaid TSMC wafers and memory NVIDIA had committed to buying was “coming at him like an avalanche.”

By funding datacenter expansion for AI startups, NVIDIA effectively created artificial demand to clear out its own surplus silicon instead of letting the supply flood the market and force GPU prices down. Those internal pressures align with earlier assessments from industry analyst Ed Zitron, who estimated that at least $200 billion worth of NVIDIA AI GPUs are sitting idle in warehouses after being purchased by cloud giants that lacked either the electrical grid capacity or immediate end-user demand to power them on. Amazon faced a similar dilemma .

Knowing that the imminent avalanche would be upon NVIDIA sooner rather than later, the company reportedly contacted TSMC to wind down its upcoming chip orders. For PC builders and hardware enthusiasts who have endured years of steep GPU and RAM pricing under the impression of severe component scarcity, the disclosures shatter the shortage narrative and expose the aggressive financial maneuvering used to keep hardware prices elevated.

While Jensen can’t be faulted for making these moves because he was keeping the best interests of the company in mind, it’s a stab in the back for gamers and hardware owners who are unable to locate any mouth-watering deals for GPUs or memory because of the perceived shortage.

News Source: The Wall Street Journal

item.title: TCL Showcases World’s Fastest Laptop OLED Panel At 360 Hz On Lenovo Legion Prototype
item.description:
Chinese display maker TCL CSOT has demonstrated a blazing-fast OLED display on a Lenovo Legion laptop prototype that boasts a 360 Hz refresh rate at 1440p resolution.

New 16-inch 1440p Inkjet-Printed OLED Panel Pushed Beyond 300 Hz on Lenovo Laptop

A few months ago, Samsung just pushed laptop OLEDs to 300 Hz at 2.5K resolution, bringing more fluidity to gaming laptops. Now, Chinese display maker TCL CSOT has joined the race and has demonstrated what could become the world's fastest OLED panel for the laptops. This was showcased in a Lenovo Legion gaming laptop prototype at the DTC 2026 event.

The laptop reportedly features a 360 Hz OLED display, and this isn't your conventional OLED panel, but an inkjet-printed OLED that uses precision nozzles to spray liquid organic materials directly into defined subpixel trenches. This not only reduces the production cost but also delivers enhanced text clarity. This display offers a 16-inch screen size with a 2560 x 1440p resolution and delivers 100% DCI-P3 color coverage and a brightness of up to 500 nits.

The most notable feature is surely its 360 Hz refresh rate operation that is blazing-fast and ideal for competitive gaming. It's also a significant jump over the previous 240 Hz IJP OLED panel that TCL CSTO supplied for Lenovo's Legion R9000P laptop earlier this year. That said, hitting 360 FPS at 1440p resolution will be a challenge and is particularly difficult on laptops because laptop-grade GPUs are way weaker than their desktop counterparts.

Still, given that the monitor market is rapidly advancing with displays hitting 1000+ Hz refresh rates, the laptops were already way behind in this area, and with the introduction of 360 Hz displays, enthusiasts will have more options to explore. TCL CSOT says that it is working with its partners and that mass production of the new 360 Hz OLED panel could begin soon.

However, the company hasn't provided any information regarding the release date, pricing, or final hardware configuration for the Lenovo Legion laptop it showcased.

News Source: NoteBookCheck

item.title: NVIDIA Founder Jensen Huang’s Alleged Spy Associate Alice Huang Was Deeply Tied To Another Chinese Firm With Access To Banned NVIDIA Chips, Says Report
item.description:
A new entity tied to Alice Huang, the Chinese executive at the heart of the scandal that led to the resignation of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, disclosed banned NVIDIA GPUs as part of collateral offered by the holding company for financing in 2025, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The new details share another link with Alice Huang, whose firm Megaspeed has already been probed for supplying banned NVIDIA AI chips to China.

Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's Partner Alice Huang's Holding Company Installed Banned NVIDIA AI Chips In Shanghai Data Center, Says Report

While reports suggest that the US intelligence community is unconvinced that Alice Huang, the associate of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, was a spy, her links to transporting banned GPUs to China are nevertheless present in Bloomberg's analysis of filings with Chinese regulators.

In a report , the publication shares that a holding company called Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group Co. ended up gaining access to servers purchased by Aperia Cloud from Dell. Aperia's CEO is facing charges for fraud related to the smuggling of NVIDIA GPUs to China.

A Longteng unit (Shanghai Longjie Yaoteng) then used these servers as part of a group of equipment as collateral for financing, says the report, which adds that Alice founded Longteng in 2016 and relinquished shares in 2017.

The details about the holding company, which is tied to a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed, come as the Southeast Asian nation of Malaysia further tightens GPU rules. Amidst the firestorm created by the former NVIDIA CEO, Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani shared earlier today that his country was evaluating current laws to determine whether they could target GPU re-exports to comply with the US sanctions.

US lawmakers are also advancing legislation to prevent Chinese AI companies from accessing restricted chips remotely, with 'footprints' of the banned Blackwell GPUs discovered in forensic analysis of leading Chinese AI models.

While Bloomberg also claims that servers manufactured by Super Micro, using the H100 or H200 chips, were also part of the regulatory disclosure, the firm asserted that it did not directly make any such sales.

Super Micro has long faced scrutiny for similar shipments. Individuals tied to the firm were charged by the Justice Department in March for diverting restricted chips to China. However, the firm's statement claimed that the actions of the indicted were against its rules and policies and in line with US law.

item.title: Astro Bot is the First PlayStation 5 Game to Get an Unofficial PC Port, Complete With NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution and Frame Generation Support
item.description:
With so many console games getting native PC ports, including the recently released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , and with work on AnyPS5 continuing, it was only a matter of time before the first unofficial PlayStation 5 ports would appear. And the honor has gone to Astro Bot , the 2024 Game of the Year , which has now hit PC complete with some advanced features, including full NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution and Frame Generation support.

"A personal research project: running my own legally owned PS5 copy of Astro Bot (PPSA21567, v01.019.000) natively on Windows, with NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution, DLSS (Multi) Frame Generation and Reflex added on top," wrote imnotsharingmyname on GitHub . The developer further outlined the features of the project, which, as already stated, is a proper native port:

  • AnyPS5 : relinks the game's own x86-64 code into a Windows .exe ( AstroBot.exe ). The PS5 system libraries (kernel, libc, pad, audio, save data and so on) are reimplemented natively as Windows modules.
  • AstroHybrid : the PS5 GPU side (AGC command buffers, shaders, VideoOut) is handled by a GPU stack taken from KytyPS5 and built as kyty_gpu.dll . It translates the GPU work to Vulkan and is loaded by the native .exe .
  • NVIDIA RTX layer (new) : the game's own temporal upscale pass is found at run time and its inputs (colour, depth, motion vectors, jitter, camera matrices) are handed to DLSS and to DLSS Frame Generation through NVIDIA Streamline 2.14.16 on Vulkan .

While it is exciting that Astro Bot has finally hit PC , even after Sony decided to stop porting its single-player games, the unofficial port still needs some work to match the original PlayStation 5 release's 60 FPS performance on low- and mid-range hardware.

According to the benchmarks provided by the port's developer, in the demanding Sky Garden , the port hits 32-34 FPS on a system powered by a Ryzen 5 5500 ( 6 cores / 12 threads ) CPU, RTX 5060 8 GB GPU, and 32 GB RAM at 1440p resolution, while hitting the 40–50 FPS range in other areas. With Frame Generation , the game runs comfortably at 60 FPS , while Multi Frame Generation bumps this to 128 FPS .

With full support for all controllers, including DualSense , Xbox , Switch Pro , and compatible generic pads, and settings getting automatically picked depending on the hardware, this unofficial PC port of Astro Bot could not only become the best way to enjoy one of the best PlayStation 5 exclusives to date, but may also pave the way for other native ports of other exclusives, including the Demon's Souls remake and Gran Turismo 7 , which could both benefit from extra features not available via the KytyPS5 emulator.

item.title: DeepSeek And Moonshot AI Models Appear To Carry Hidden NVIDIA Blackwell Fingerprints In Their Starting Weights, Pointing To Training Clusters Of 3,000 To 4,500 GPUs
item.description:
With chip tensions between the US and China experiencing another surge following former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure from the firm, forensic analysis conducted by Uemployment Labs suggests that several Chinese AI models might have relied on thousands of NVIDIA's latest Blackwell AI GPUs for their training run.

The AI lab attempted to match hardware fingerprints linked specifically to the Blackwell chips by reverse engineering AI model weights and recovering the thread count for the processors that initialized the AI model's training run.

Top Chinese AI Models Developed By DeepSeek & Moonshot Might Have Relied On NVIDIA's Blackwell GPUs During Initialization Training, Says Researcher

While Unemployment Labs' report claims to show that some Chinese labs were able to access the advanced Blackwell GPUs, it does add that the evidence is not to evaluate whether Blackwell gPU export control regulations were violated.

The data, which relies on matching the hardware imprint of each chip with the imprint generated via analyzing a model's weights, does, however, suggest that individual training runs utilized clusters ranging between 4,500 and 3,000 Blackwell GPUs, with combined multi-model footprints reaching upwards of 12,000 chips across participating labs.

The researchers analyzed the AI models' published weights and used these to figure out the seed that generated the initial model weights at the time DeepSeek and others started model training.

Model weights, also called parameters, enable an AI model to transform input into output. Most weights transform throughout the training phase, but the initial set can be determined by some static weights, says Depue.

A seed is a value fed into a number generator to produce a set of numbers that are called initial weights. The initial set of numbers is locked into a matrix pattern dependent on the AI GPU design architecture used at the time of training initialization. DuPue claims to have compared the pattern of static weights in the AI models against the initialization patterns produced by the streaming multiprocessor (SM) layouts of NVIDIA’s Hopper and Blackwell GPUs to conclude that the models started their training runs with the NVIDIA chips.

Because each type of AI chip has a fixed number of processing cores, that hardware layout dictates the exact grid pattern used to place starting random numbers into an AI model before training begins. Each GPU architecture has a different SM layout, which makes the GPU class identifiable if one looks deep enough at an AI model's weights.

Chinese AI Labs Might Have Used As Many As 22,000 Blackwell GPUs For Training Initialization, Says Report

By relying on pattern matching, the researchers conclude that several thousand Blackwell GPUs were used by DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Inclusion AI. The estimate ranges from 7,000 to 22,000 GPUs cumulatively for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the DeepSeek-V4-Pro, the MiniMax-M3, Kimi K3 and the Ling-3.1-flash AI models and is highly dependent on the time of the training run, GPU usage efficiency and other factors.

The 22,000 figure assumes that the models did not train on the same Blackwell Cluster. It is quite modest, compared to, for instance, Elon Musk's plan to bring more than a million of such chips online by 2026 end .

Even for the few chips that the Chinese AI labs were able to procure for their training initialization, the report cautions:

"Notably, our findings provide technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, but do not establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated."

While NVIDIA's Blackwell AI GPUs are export-controlled items and cannot be sold to China, Chinese AI labs can access them remotely via GPU clusters. Similarly, Commerce Department guidance issued in May this year stated that the restrictions also applied to selling to subsidiaries of Chinese companies typically located in Singapore or Malaysia.

The recent saga surrounding NVIDIA's founder and former CEO, Jensen Huang, has also brought fresh spotlight for chip exports to China. Legislation in Congress seeks to target remote access while Chinese firms are already rushing to secure orders before the rules are further tightened.

NVIDIA's CUDA stack provides it a key advantage in the AI chip industry as it was the only mature GPU platform at the time deep learning grew in popularity. However, some, such as Anthropic, have claimed that switching to AMD GPUs is now just a matter of weeks for some applications.

The trail also goes cold with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, as the newest AI model from the Chinese lab has a new architecture. This architecture masks the GPU initialization footprint, with Defue noting:

"Likewise, weights initialized on an ordinary processor rather than a GPU leave no GPU fingerprint; several of Alibaba’s Qwen3 models were initialized this way, and thus leave no trace of which GPUs were used to train them. We also found no fingerprint in Meituan’s LongCat-2.0, which the company says was trained on “AI ASIC superpods,” or in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, despite an exhaustive search."

item.title: Quick Spectral Super Resolution Comes Soon to Six PS5 Games: Spider-Man 2, CONTROL Resonant, The Finals, ARC Raiders, No Man’s Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam
item.description:
Sony announced today that six PlayStation 5 games have added or are about to add support for Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) , the lightweight AI upscaler derived from PS5 Pro's PSSR and originally released in October . The games are Marvel's Spider-Man 2 , CONTROL Resonant , The Finals , ARC Raiders , No Man's Sky , and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam .

Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now! item.title: After NVIDIA Pushes Out Jensen Huang, Alice Huang’s Spy Credentials Suddenly Start To Crack, Leading To Pronouncements Of A Coup
item.description:
It's a compelling narrative: Jensen Huang, a champion of open-source AI models and an advocate of retaining a sizable compute footprint within China, was perceived as a threat by the powers that be, who then engineered his ignominious exit from NVIDIA by painting his extensively photographed relationship with Alice Huang as a honeytrap, which we are to believe was engineered by the Chinese intelligence agencies.

Interestingly, this narrative started to crack within hours of Jensen Huang's resignation as the CEO of NVIDIA , further bolstering the thesis that this entire melodrama was the result of a targeted hit job.

Given the breadth of available evidence, you can at best accuse Jensen Huang of negligence, and that too of a fairly marginal kind

Up until Thursday, the U.S. national security establishment was baying for blood. The Economist labeled Jensen Huang a "fool" with a "catastrophic failure of judgment." The New York Times repeatedly asserted that Alice Huang was in cahoots with China's Ministry of State Security and then declared her a "spy" around 30 times across 11 reports , all based off a single memo from Marco Rubio that no one seems to have actually seen.

And yet, shortly after Jensen Huang resigned from his post as the CEO of NVIDIA, the U.S. Attorney General, Todd Blanche, declared that the Department of Justice (DOJ) has reached no conclusion on whether Alice Huang was acting on behalf of China's intelligence agencies:

"Your first question assumes something that I’ve never said and that I don’t know to be true. So you assume that DOJ learns that she is, in fact, a spy. I’m not. Nobody said that. I certainly haven’t said that."

"All I said a minute ago, and all that I think I will say, is that of course DOJ is investigating, looking at it. So there’s no conclusions reached by the Department of Justice, or by me, or by Director Patel, around who she is or is not."

So, let me get this straight: there is no conclusive proof of a honeytrap at this stage, and the DOJ has made no such determination. At best, Alice Huang can be characterized right now as an entrepreneur who excels in operating within the grey market . And yet, Jensen Huang was charged and condemned within the media even before NVIDIA's own inquiry could be concluded. Last I checked, our society still operates under a presumption of innocence until proven guilty.

Now, let's tackle the smuggling angle. According to The Information, Jensen Huang’s long-standing ties to Alice Huang facilitated over $7 billion in NVIDIA chip sales to China through a corporate network, which included firms like Shanghai Century Litong and Megaspeed. Critically though, the report notes that the network acquired and distributed approximately 240,000 units of NVIDIA's A- and H-series chips.

Do note that while NVIDIA's A100 and H100 GPUs were restricted from direct shipment to China starting in late 2022, modified versions like the A800 and H800 chips remained legal for export until October 2023. Subsequent policy shifts under the Trump administration also conditionally eased certain restrictions on older or specific tiers of these chips, including the H20 and H200 GPUs.

Even if we assume that the entirety of this volume spanned GPU variants that were explicitly banned under U.S. export controls, it would still make up just around 4 percent of NVIDIA's A- and H-series revenue of around $184 billion between its FY 2021 and FY 2025 (cumulative data center segment sales of $195.03 billion less the $11.00 billion in initial Blackwell sales).

So, Alice Huang supposedly held tremendous sway over Jensen Huang, and even then she could only manage to direct just 4 percent of NVIDIA's total A- and H-series chip sales towards China in the most adverse reading of this situation?

And yet, we now supposedly have another smoking gun, courtesy of a former OpenAI employee, Will Depue, who has "found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China."

As per a tabulation by Depue, even the largest Blackwell-based Chinese training clusters at these AI labs span just 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. And, even If we assume that China's top four AI labs have a cluster of 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each, the total 12,000-GPU stash would still correspond to just around 14.4 MW of compute vs. China's total compute capacity of 24 GW ! Clearly, export controls have not failed, and whatever fraction of NVIDIA's Blackwell GPUs that have managed to enter China did so as a result of predictable and perverse incentives from the associated black market.

These volumes are so negligible that an inquiry and a small number of remedial steps should have sufficed. But no, here we witnessed Jensen Huang's full-fledged character assassination, and all but declared him a national security threat just so Anthropic and OpenAI can establish their hoped-for duopoly.

The powers that be played their cards well: got rid of the biggest proponent of open-source models and an advocate of retaining a compute footprint within China in one fell swoop. This is a pyrrhic victory, however, as we've just handed China all the incentive in the world to gun for self-sufficiency on AI compute, as DeepSeek and Huawei are now attempting with the upcoming V5-series models .

Finally, Jensen Huang's love life is toxic. But so is that of Elon Musk, President Trump, and a sizable number of U.S. senators and House members. You don't see any of these august personalities resigning? Why single out Jensen Huang?

Of course, a time may come when we have enough evidence to convict the former CEO of NVIDIA. But that's the point: why socially ostracize him when there simply is not enough evidence of malfeasance right now?

Make no mistake. A public coup was just staged in America, all in a bid to herald a dystopian future, one where the Anthropic-OpenAI duopoly reigns supreme.

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sells 5 Million in Four Days, Yet Former Nintendo Leads Say The Series Sold “Like Nothing” Before Breath of the Wild
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has become a smashing success, selling over 5 million copies in only four days of availability, but the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of one of the best games ever released had the real risk of never seeing the light of day. According to former Nintendo of America marketing leads Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang , the franchise was going through its darkest days before the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , with new games selling like nothing.

"The series was in dire straits. They were selling like nothing," said Yang during the latest episode of the Kit & Krysta Podcast . "Yeah, I remember I was going to the focus groups. It was a really dark moment," added Ellis . "The feedback is the fan base is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players. We had so much data of like every game, the interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller. They had to do something drastic."

Looking at the timeline, it's very likely that The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword contributed a lot to the dark age of the franchise, which required the massive open-world overhaul of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild . The first 3D entry in the series built from the ground up for the Wii system sold only 3.67 million units, a disappointing figure considering the 101 million Wii systems sold worldwide. Making this figure even more dire is how the Nintendo Switch HD remaster released in 2021 outsold the original in just a few months, benefiting from the massive popularity of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild .

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake enjoying such incredible popularity, it will be interesting to see where Eiji Aonuma and his team will take the franchise. While both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom are incredible games, they can sometimes feel too big, a feeling that's highlighted well by the immaculate pacing of the Ocarina of Time remake, granted by the great design of Hyrule . Regardless of which direction will define the next era of the franchise, there's no denying that the dark days are indeed over for Link and Zelda .

item.title: Escape from Tarkov Director Nikita Buyanov Says the Console Version Will Be Announced Next Year, “100%”, but It Won’t Be Ready

The PC game still doesn't support controllers, so it's clear there's still work to be done in that area. Meanwhile, though, the protoextraction shooter continues to be updated, with features such as:
